conflicts.description: The community technical chart's switch matrix prints Laser Kick, while the retained runtime calls the same address Kickback. The combined label preserves both terms. Resolution path: a legible copy of Data East's own printed Laser War switch list, which the retained 42-page image-only manual archive cannot supply because its typeset chart text is absent from the page images, would give the factory name for this address. Unresolved.

The community technical chart prints a physical Right E.O.S. switch and flipper circuit, while FLIP4746 and the retained script use address 46 as right-flipper button state. The retained sources do not reconcile the physical contact and its polarity with that controller-facing behavior.
conflicts.rationale: An end-of-stroke contact exists so a physical coil's power winding is cut before it burns, and a recreation has no coil to protect. This platform models no EOS at all -- the driver macro uses FLIP_SWNO without FLIP_SOL, so core.c's EOS simulation never runs -- and PinMAME publishes cabinet-button state at this address instead. Which of the two names belongs on it cannot change any table. The physical contact's polarity goes with it: a consumer reads the published button state, never the EOS contact, and the separate question of which physical winding each synthetic 45-48 state drives is recorded on its own at conflict.synthetic-flipper-public-state. The record is kept because it explains this address's conflicted provenance; it is not an outstanding question.

conflicts.description: The community technical chart prints a physical Left E.O.S. switch and flipper circuit, while FLIP4746 and the retained script use address 47 as left-flipper button state. The retained sources do not reconcile the physical contact and its polarity with that controller-facing behavior.

conflicts.description: The printed lamp matrix assigns address 8 to Return To Base. The retained script has no lamp-8 callback and uses its l8a-v tower helpers under solenoid 5 instead, so no physical lamp-8 placement is asserted. Resolution path: a photograph of an unrestored playfield showing where the Return To Base insert sits and that the address-8 branch feeds it, or a second independently authored known-working Laser War recreation that binds lamp 8 to its own object. Unresolved.

The community technical chart literally prints Red Target (Right) at lamp 26, duplicating lamp 18. The retained table places amber l26 beside the yellow target bank and the same chart names switch 32 Yellow Target (Right), so the structured semantic label remains Yellow Target (Right) while the printed disagreement is preserved verbatim. Resolution path: a corrected revision of the 2021 Inkochnito technical chart from its author, or a photograph of an unrestored playfield showing which target insert the address-26 lamp branch actually feeds. Unresolved.

The community technical chart calls Mars Yellow device type 23-800, while the otherwise matching Mars Red and Mars Blue rows say #89. Pinned s11.c independently treats the yellow, red and blue Mars flashers as one two-bulb-per-colour group, so kind flasher is the documented resolution; the printed 23-800 disagreement is retained verbatim and remains first-class provenance. Resolution path: a photograph of an unrestored playfield's Mars Yellow position showing whether the chart's Vio-Blu CPU CN11-7 branch feeds #89 bulbs like its Mars Red and Mars Blue partners or a 23-800 coil, or a legible copy of Data East's own printed coil table for this game, which the retained image-only manual archive does not supply. Unresolved.

The community technical chart types public 4, 5, 7, and 8 as additional #89 flashers, public 6 as a disputed 23-800 Mars circuit, public 29 as a 23-800 knocker, and public 30-32 as unfitted. Pinned s11.c instead applies #89-bulb PWM typing only to public 1-3 and then to all public 25-32. The semantic mapping follows the game-specific chart and retained runtime while preserving the emulator output-typing disagreement. Resolution path: a corrected lwar_ output-typing block in upstream src/wpc/s11.c, which a PinMAME contributor can submit against the chart's printed per-row device types, together with a LibPinMAME gameplay trace against a legal lwar_a83 ROM observing whether public 30-32 ever carry state, since the chart proves rows 6R, 7R and 8R carry no physical load but PinMAME can still publish those addresses. Unresolved.

The community technical chart numbers Blue Pop, Yellow Pop, Left Sling, Red Pop, Right Sling and the unfitted driver as Coil No. 17-22. It does not print SP identities. Interpreting pinned s11.c's shared SS handler comments and Data East offsets produces a different physical-device order at public 17-22. The definition follows the game-specific chart as a conflicted working mapping and marks all six outputs and five mechanisms conflicted until a LibPinMAME trace observes the public pulses. Resolution path: that trace has to be a gameplay run rather than a diagnostic sweep - boot a legal lwar_a83 ROM in the implemented harness, start a ball, and close each pop-bumper and slingshot switch in turn while watching public 17-22 - because the retained Data East alpha Coil Test traces show the ROM's automatic cycle never pulsing those addresses. Unresolved.

PinMAME synthesizes public power/hold states 45-48 for FLIP4746 even though Laser War's physical flippers use cabinet-wired dual-winding assemblies rather than four distinct CPU driver outputs. The printed EOS labels and retained button-state callbacks do not establish a winding-by-winding public mapping, so all four virtual states remain conflicted. Resolution path: a LibPinMAME harness trace against a legal lwar_a83 ROM holding each flipper button and reading the idle and held state of 45-48, paired with a bench continuity check on an unrestored machine's dual-winding flipper assemblies showing which winding the button feed energises and which remains energised past end of stroke. Unresolved.

mechanisms.behavior: The retained script initializes all three trough switches active. Pulsing the ball-trough eject moves the front ball from switch 12 into the shooter lane; the remaining balls advance toward switch 12.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball closes the outhole switch. The outhole coil kicks that ball into the three-ball trough; the script explicitly clears switch 13 when it fires.
mechanisms.label: Outhole feeder

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer captures one ball, asserts switch 25, and the red-eject coil kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Red eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer captures one ball, asserts switch 33, and the yellow-eject coil kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Yellow eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer captures one ball, asserts switch 38, and the blue-eject coil kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Blue eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Public output 15 controls a 24 VDC Laser Kick relay; its downstream 23-900 local kickback coil is not a separate PinMAME output. The retained runtime arms the local kick while the relay is active, then switch 17 triggers it. The empty actuator list avoids misidentifying the relay as the mechanical actuator.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane kickback

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 15 when the left sling surface fires. The community technical chart numbers the left-sling circuit Coil No. 19 at Q10. The shared-source permutation suggests a different public address, so this working binding remains conflicted pending a LibPinMAME trace.
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 14 when the right sling surface fires. The community technical chart numbers the right-sling circuit Coil No. 21 at Q12. The shared-source permutation happens to agree at this address, but the six-address contract remains conflicted pending a LibPinMAME trace.
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 43 on a red pop-bumper hit. The community technical chart numbers the red-pop circuit Coil No. 20 at Q11. The shared-source permutation suggests a different public address, so this working binding remains conflicted pending a LibPinMAME trace.
mechanisms.label: Red pop bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 44 on a yellow pop-bumper hit. The community technical chart numbers the yellow-pop circuit Coil No. 18 at Q9. The shared-source permutation suggests a different public address, so this working binding remains conflicted pending a LibPinMAME trace.
mechanisms.label: Yellow pop bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 45 on a blue pop-bumper hit. The community technical chart numbers the blue-pop circuit Coil No. 17 at Q8. The shared-source permutation agrees at this address, but the six-address contract remains conflicted pending a LibPinMAME trace.
mechanisms.label: Blue pop bumper

mechanisms.behavior: PinMAME synthesizes lower-left power/hold outputs and the script fires the left flipper callback. The technical chart proves one physical dual-winding flipper circuit, but its printed EOS label conflicts with the runtime button-state use and does not establish a complete physical polarity claim.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: PinMAME synthesizes lower-right power/hold outputs and the script fires the right flipper callback. The technical chart proves one physical dual-winding flipper circuit, but its printed EOS label conflicts with the runtime button-state use and does not establish a complete physical polarity claim.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: A passive spinner pulses switch 27 as it turns; it has no CPU actuator.
mechanisms.label: Red spinner

mechanisms.behavior: A passive spinner pulses switch 51 as it turns; it has no CPU actuator.
mechanisms.label: Yellow spinner

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the ramp closes switch 29 and follows the retained table's wire-ramp path back toward the shooter-side return. No motor or diverter is scripted.
mechanisms.label: Wire ramp and return path

mechanisms.behavior: The spring plunger is player-driven. A launched ball traverses shooter-lane switch 52; there is no physical CPU shooter coil.
mechanisms.label: Manual plunger and shooter lane

src/wpc/degames.c lines 9-16 and 122-145 define Laser War's Data East CPU Rev 1 hardware, display board, GEN_DE GameData, FLIP4746 and three-driver clone tree; src/wpc/s11.c lines 537-554 apply Data East special-output offsets {3,4,5,1,0,2}, lines 618-623 connect the six PIA handlers, and lines 714-749 comment them SS6, SS5, SST2, SST3, SS1 and SS4. Treating those shared comments as physical special-solenoid identities produces an order that conflicts with the game-specific 17-22 community chart. Lines 1130-1134 type only public 1-3 and all 25-32 as #89 bulbs, which conflicts with the chart's additional left-bank flashers, right-bank knocker, and unfitted circuits. INITGAMES11 leaves the inversion mask zero-initialized

sources.locator: Community-compiled one-page 2021 Inkochnito Laser War technical chart, acquired from https://www.pinballrebel.com/pinball/cards/Tech_Charts/Data_East_Laser_War_Tech_Chart.pdf. It prints the complete switch and lamp matrices, Coil No. rows 1L-22, driver transistors, wire colours, connector pins, flipper circuits, and fuse list. It is secondary evidence, not a Data East factory manual.
